A genuinely idle function would keep its metric (metrics persist once created) and its datapoints and Sum would fall toward zero. CORROBORATION ON A SECOND AXIS: the count moved from 141,685 to 141,686 between two reads an hour apart, so the number is tracking live traffic rather than a cached figure. STRUCTURAL EVIDENCE THAT THE Z-S124 TRAP CANNOT APPLY HERE AT ALL: this function is not Lambda@Edge and is structurally ineligible to be -- its role opal-portal-lambda-role trusts lambda.amazonaws.com ONLY, while the control lambda-edge-execution-role carries edgelambda.amazonaws.com, and CloudFront rejects an association whose role lacks it. REGION DENOMINATOR, printed although the evidence is not log-based and the viewer-region trap is void for a non-edge function: 1 region, us-east-1, log group /aws/lambda/opal-session-analytics with no region-prefixed siblings.

acceptance.invocation: Read src/auth.ts and the deployed auth.js at source; measured container lifetime from aws logs describe-log-streams (creation to lastEventTimestamp); read infra/aws/lambda/lib/authkeys/jwtPublicKeys.mjs; searched the project deliverables for an existing rotation runbook
acceptance.output_evidence: ANSWERED THE SECOND WAY, EXPLICITLY: redeploy-per-rotation is required today. auth.js:24-26 is `if (cachedPublicKey) return cachedPublicKey;` then a GetSecretValue on opal/auth/jwt-public-key -- module-level, no TTL, no invalidation, one slot. A warm container verifies against the OLD public key and rejects tokens signed with the new private key for as long as it lives. THERE IS NO RUNBOOK TO AMEND AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND: TO-OP-S-10 reads staged and the dual-key overlap runbook is its own deliverable; the project's only rotation runbook is TO-OP-S-3's, for the ORIGIN secret. So the answer is a committed note (e70ca4e244) DELIVERED to TO-OP-S-10's assignee as msg 20226 -- amending a runbook that does not exist would satisfy the criterion's words and none of its purpose. AND A CORRECTION TO THIS FACE'S OWN FRAMING, MEASURED: 'breaks PERMANENTLY, with no mechanism left to repair it' overstates it. The cache is bounded by CONTAINER LIFETIME -- median 5.6 min, p90 52.3, p99 138.0, max observed 143.0 (2.4 h), from 107 measurable spans of 200 streams sampled with NextToken present, so a FLOOR not a census and biased toward recently-active containers. The true shape is a PARTIAL, SILENT, SELF-CLEARING OUTAGE OF UNBOUNDED TAIL DURATION, which is worse than permanent breakage in one respect: permanent breakage gets NOTICED, while a partial outage that clears on its own is absorbed as 'some 401s during the rotation' and never traced to this consumer. THE REFRESH PATH EXISTS AND NEEDS DEPLOYING RATHER THAN DESIGNING: jwtPublicKeys.mjs is two-slot with JWT_KEY_TTL_MS=300000 and accepts both the secret's current bare-PEM shape and its post-rotation envelope. Its own packaging note records that the lib mirror is gated on the consumer having a src/ and that neither portal-authorizer nor auth-validator-edge has one -- session-analytics HAS one, so it is the consumer the shared remedy fits most cleanly. Deploying it is act two.
acceptance.denominator: 1 of 1 key-fetch sites in the function read at source; 107 container lifetimes measured of 200 streams sampled; 1 of 1 shared refresh libraries evaluated; 2 existing rotation runbooks checked, 0 governing this key

mutant.description: The face names S10C-AC1's instrument test as the control that must be able to fail -- an aliveness oracle that cannot say 'dead' is the one that read ZERO on a function under load. Tested by running the identical query across five functions spanning both outcomes, rather than only against the subject.
mutant.expected: If the instrument were incapable of saying 'dead', every function would return a live-looking number. If it were broken the other way, the known-live subject would read zero.
mutant.observed: Two functions returned metric-absent (auth-validator-edge, deck-generation) and three returned live counts spanning two orders of magnitude -- 141,686 / 4,459 / 2,214. The instrument distinguishes present from absent AND loud from quiet. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT MUTANT sits under S10C-AC2: the build was run twice into separate clean directories, and had the path not been repeatable the two would have differed; had the repo source not been production, both would have differed from the deployed artifact. Neither happened -- 12 of 12 identical in both directions.

determinism.method: The build was executed twice from clean state in separate directories and the outputs compared by sha256; the aliveness query was re-run an hour after the first read.
determinism.observed: Builds: 12 of 12 outputs byte-identical between runs. Aliveness: 141,685 then 141,686 an hour later -- the one-count movement is live traffic, not instability, and a frozen number would have been the suspicious result.
